setup.title: {title} · HomersLab setup
setup.foot: You can stop at any time: what you’ve chosen is kept, and you continue where you stopped. To come back later, make a new link on this machine with sudo homerslab setup link.
setup.refused.title: This link doesn’t work any more
setup.refused.lead: A setup link works once, for 30 minutes, on this machine or your home network. To make a new one, run this on the machine:
setup.error.title: Setup can’t reach HomersLab
setup.error.lead: The manager on this machine didn’t answer. Check that it runs, then try again.
setup.full.title: This machine’s disk is full
setup.full.lead: HomersLab can’t keep anything you answer until there’s room on it. Free some space on this machine, then try again.
setup.full.answer: This machine’s disk is full, so your answer wasn’t kept. Free some space on it, then continue again.
setup.error.unbuilt: This step comes with a later version of HomersLab. What you’ve chosen so far is kept.
setup.fail.server: HomersLab couldn’t save this. What you typed is still here: try again in a moment.
setup.fail.offline: This device couldn’t reach HomersLab. Check its connection, then try again: what you typed is still here.
setup.fail.moved: Setup moved on in another tab or browser. Reload to carry on from where it is now.
setup.fail.lanDone: The home network’s part of setup is done, so this can’t change here any more. Reload to carry on over the mesh.
setup.fail.mesh: This step is answered over the mesh, not on your home network.
setup.fail.refused: HomersLab didn’t take this answer. Reload this page to carry on from where setup is.
setup.fail.here: HomersLab takes setup only from this machine or your home network, on its own page. Open the link again from there.
step.welcome.title: Let’s set up HomersLab
step.welcome.lead: This machine, {host}, will run your household’s apps. It takes about 20 minutes, and you can stop at any time.
step.welcome.backLead: You stopped at {step}. What you chose then is kept.
step.welcome.need.mesh: Your mesh’s token: NetBird, Tailscale or Headscale
step.welcome.need.domain: Your domain and its DNS provider’s token
step.welcome.need.mail: The password of a mailbox HomersLab can send from
step.welcome.need.kit: A printer or a password manager, for the recovery kit
step.welcome.need.device: This laptop or your phone, to put on the mesh
step.welcome.agentSilent: The agent on this machine isn’t answering, so its facts can’t be shown yet.
fact.noTPM: None: secrets are sealed to this machine’s own key
step.you.title: What’s your name?
step.you.lead: You’ll be the household’s admin: you install apps and invite people.
step.you.name: Your name
step.you.mailHint: For alerts, and to reset your passkey.
step.you.why: Your name and a mail address, to continue.
step.you.mailInvalid: Type a mail address, like name@example.org.
step.you.nameTooLong: Your name can be 64 characters at most. An accent or an emoji can count as more than one.
step.you.nameHidden: Your name has an invisible character, or one a name can’t use, often pasted along with it. Type it again.
step.you.mailTooLong: A mail address can be 254 characters at most.
step.you.mailHidden: This mail address has an invisible character, often pasted along with it. Type it again.
step.household.title: Name your household
step.household.lead: Everyone you invite joins it. You can change its name later.
step.household.name: The household’s name
step.household.why: Give the household a name to continue.
step.household.tooLong: The household’s name can be 64 characters at most. An accent or an emoji can count as more than one.
step.household.hidden: The name has an invisible character, or one a name can’t use, often pasted along with it. Type it again.
step.signin.title: How everyone signs in
step.signin.lead: One household account and a passkey for every app, on the TV too.
step.network.title: Your private network
step.network.lead: It joins your machines and everyone’s devices, at home or away. NetBird is a good start.
step.network.cloudSub: Nothing to run yourself; free for a household.
step.network.ownSub: On a server outside your home: HomersLab never opens a port on your router.
step.network.urlHint: Such as https://netbird.example.org. A new server is set up for you; one in use asks for a token next.
step.network.urlInvalid: Type the server’s https:// address. HomersLab couldn’t reach a NetBird server there.
step.network.why: Type your NetBird server’s address to continue.
step.network.later: Tailscale and Headscale come with a later version of HomersLab.
step.network.waitTitle: Now give HomersLab NetBird’s token, on this machine
step.network.waitLead: Tokens never travel over this page. Run this in the terminal where you made the link, then paste the token:
step.network.waitWhy: Run the command on this machine first.
step.network.help: Where do I find the token?
step.network.help1: Open app.netbird.io (or your own server’s dashboard) and sign in.
step.network.help2: Go to Team › Service users and create a service user, as an admin.
step.network.help3: Open it, create a token that expires in a day, and copy it.
step.network.helpWhy: HomersLab uses it once to make its own service user and token, then forgets it. Your machines and devices never need the dashboard again.
step.network.conflictsTitle: Switch off what lets everything through?
step.network.conflictsLead: These policies in your NetBird let every device reach every machine, past the roles HomersLab gives people. Before this machine joins, HomersLab switches them off.
step.network.conflictsKept: They stay in NetBird, switched off, for you to look at. If one appears later, Admin tells you.
step.network.done: Checked: this machine is on the mesh, and the LAN no longer reaches any app.
step.domain.title: Your domain
step.domain.lead: Every app gets a name under it, like {example}, with one certificate for them all. The names answer only on the mesh.
step.domain.domainHint: From your mail address. A name under it works too, such as home.ferreira.family.
step.domain.domainInvalid: Type the domain itself, such as ferreira.family.
step.domain.infomaniakSub: HomersLab uses Infomaniak’s API, with a token you make for it.
step.domain.rfc2136Sub: BIND, Knot or PowerDNS, through RFC 2136 with a TSIG key.
step.domain.serverInvalid: Type the server’s name or address, with its port if it isn’t 53.
step.domain.keyNameInvalid: Type the key’s name, as your DNS server knows it.
step.domain.only: HomersLab writes only _acme-challenge records, and one _homerslab record that lists them, for one wildcard certificate: the apps’ names never appear in public certificate logs. Nothing else in your zone changes, mail records included.
step.domain.waitTitle: Now give HomersLab the DNS token, on this machine
step.domain.waitLead: Tokens never travel over this page. Run this in the terminal where you made the link, then paste the token. The certificate takes a minute or two:
step.domain.waiting: Waiting for the token and the certificate…
step.domain.waitWhy: Run the command on this machine first.
step.domain.help: Where do I find the token?
step.domain.helpInfomaniak2: Go to Your profile › Developer › API tokens.
step.domain.helpInfomaniak3: Create a token with the domain scope, and copy it.
step.domain.helpRfc21361: On your DNS server, make a TSIG key that may update this zone, and only this zone.
step.domain.helpRfc21362: Copy the key’s secret: the base64 text after secret in its configuration.
step.domain.helpWhy: The command shows where the token goes before it reads it. HomersLab keeps it sealed on this machine and never shows it again.
step.domain.done: Checked: the certificate for *.{domain} is issued. Admin answers at {admin}, over the mesh only.
step.mail.title: Sending mail
step.mail.lead: HomersLab writes invites, passkey resets and alerts.
step.kit.title: Your recovery kit
step.kit.lead: Enough to restore everything on new hardware, even without HomersLab.
step.join.title: Put this device on the mesh
step.join.lead: Admin and your passkey live at names that answer only on the mesh. Once this device is on it, you continue there.
step.join.milestoneSub: The first half of setup is done.
step.join.why: Put this device or your phone on the mesh first.
step.passkey.title: Create your passkey
step.done.title: You’re all set
